== Ecology ==

Beavers live in freshwater ecosystems such as rivers, streams, lakes and ponds. Beavers can be found in a number of freshwater habitats, such as rivers, streams, lakes and ponds. When building dams, beavers alter the paths of streams and rivers, allowing for the creation of extensive wetland habitats. These ponds can increase the productivity of freshwater ecosystems by accumulating nitrogen in sediments. In a study of Wyoming streams and rivers, watercourses with beavers had 75 times as many ducks as those without. Beavers prefer slower moving streams, typically with a gradient (steepness) of one percent, though they have been recorded using streams with gradients as high as 15 percent. Beavers are found in wider streams more often than in narrower ones. === Infrastructure ===

In Europe, beavers were reduced to fragmented populations, with combined population numbers being estimated at 1,200 individuals for the Rhône of France, the Elbe in Germany, southern Norway, the Neman river and Dnieper Basin in Belarus, and the Voronezh river in Russia. In 2020, the total Eurasian beaver population in Europe was estimated at over one million. As of 2019, the introduced population of North American beavers in Finland has been moving closer to the habitat of the Eurasian beaver. Protections have allowed the beaver population on the continent to rebound to an estimated 6–12 million by the late 20th century; still far lower than the originally estimated 60–400 million North American beavers before the fur trade. River ecosystems are part of larger watershed networks or catchments, where smaller headwater streams drain into mid-size streams, which progressively drain into larger river networks.
